sections.label: Macroeconomic update and ministerial statements
sections.summary: The speaker will update on the macroeconomic situation and the Government's approach on inflation, fuel duties and household support, answering listed questions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, I will give an update on the macroeconomic situation and explain the Government's approach on inflation, fuel duties, and support for households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Together, our Ministerial Statements will answer Question Nos 1 to 15 and also Question Nos 14 to 16 and 29 to 30 for Written Answer in today's Order Paper.

sections.label: Global inflation higher for longer
sections.summary: Hopes that global inflationary pressures would ease in 2022 gave way to expectations of higher inflation for longer due to the war in Ukraine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the start of 2022, there were some initial hopes that global inflationary pressures would ease over the course of the year as the supply situation improved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But with the war in Ukraine, it is now likely that global inflation will be higher for longer.

sections.label: Oil and gas prices staying high
sections.summary: Building new infrastructure and bringing additional oil and gas production to market takes time, so oil and gas prices are expected to remain high for some time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Furthermore, it will take time for any new infrastructure to be built and additional oil and gas production to be brought to market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We must, therefore, expect oil and gas prices to remain high for some time.

sections.label: MAS raised exchange rate band
sections.summary: MAS pre-emptively raised the rate of appreciation of its exchange rate policy band in October last year and in an off-cycle move in January this year to dampen inflationary pressures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, MAS had pre-emptively raised the rate of appreciation of its exchange rate policy band in October last year and also in an off-cycle move in January this year, to help dampen inflationary pressures.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers disbursement
sections.summary: The $100 CDC Vouchers for every Singaporean household will be disbursed by the middle of next month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, the $100 CDC Vouchers for every Singaporean household will be disbursed by the middle of next month.

sections.label: Household rebates and business support
sections.summary: The passage details U-Save and S&CC rebates, other household help, a handout schedule, and bringing forward the Small Business Recovery Grant for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To illustrate, households living in 4-room HDB flats will receive $150 in U-Save rebates this month, and that is equivalent to about a full month's worth of their utility bills, on average.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But the rest of the U-Save and S&CC rebates will be disbursed in the coming quarters – in July and October this year, and in January next year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, for the whole of Financial Year (FY) 2022, households living in 4-room flats, to give an illustration, will receive about four months of rebates on their utility bills, and that is even accounting for the higher electricity prices, and two-and-a-half months of rebates on their S&CC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We also have other forms of help for households, including top-ups to the Child Development Account, Edusave Account, or Post-Secondary Education Account of every Singaporean child, as well as the GST Voucher in terms of cash and MediSave top-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will continue to ensure that these are disbursed to Singaporeans in a timely manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And, Mr Speaker, with your permission, I would like to distribute a handout, which will provide a schedule of the various support measures that households can expect in FY2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For businesses, I will bring forward the disbursement of the Small Business Recovery Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This provides up to $10,000 for SMEs most affected by COVID-19 restrictions over the past year.

sections.label: ComCare SMTA minimum support duration
sections.summary: Social Service Offices will provide at least six months' support for new ComCare SMTA clients applying between April and September this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In particular, the Social Service Offices, or SSOs, will provide a minimum duration of six months' support for all new ComCare Short- to Medium-Term Assistance (SMTA) clients who apply between April and September this year; so, a minimum duration of six months' support for ComCare SMTA.

sections.label: CCC ComCare Fund and Self-Help Groups
sections.summary: The speaker will top up the CCC ComCare Fund by $5 million over five years and give $12 million over four years to Self-Help Groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As announced at Budget 2022, I will top up the CCC ComCare Fund by $5 million over five years and provide a total of $12 million over four years to our Self-Help Groups.

sections.label: Tangible help for Singaporeans' needs
sections.summary: These measures extend tangible help to Singaporeans for needs including utility bills, children's education and daily essentials, with more targeted help for lower-income groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Through these measures, we are extending concrete tangible help directly to Singaporeans to cope with their different areas of needs, including their utility bills, children's education and daily essentials, and we are providing more targeted help for the lower-income groups.

sections.label: Further action if situation worsens
sections.summary: The Government will not hesitate to take further actions to protect jobs and help households and businesses with increased costs if the situation worsens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As the Government has assured this House previously, if the situation worsens, we will not hesitate to take further actions to protect jobs and to help households and businesses deal with the increased costs.

sections.label: Labour and carbon as permanent constraints
sections.summary: Labour and carbon are permanent, not temporary, constraints for the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: In short, labour and carbon are permanent – not temporary – constraints for our economy.

sections.label: Inflation during 1970s oil crises
sections.summary: During the 1970s oil crises, Singapore's inflation peaked at 30% year-on-year in the first half of 1974 and around 10% in the second quarter of 1980.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: During the oil crises of the 1970s, Singapore's inflation rate peaked as high as 30% year-on-year in the first half of 1974 and around 10% in the second quarter of 1980.

sections.label: Standby LNG Facility established
sections.summary: A Standby LNG Facility was established since October last year for gencos to draw from during natural gas supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since October last year, we have established a Standby LNG Facility (SLF), which gencos can draw from to generate electricity in the event of disruptions to their natural gas supplies.

sections.label: Average USEP first quarter
sections.summary: The average USEP for the first quarter of this year stabilised to around $360 per MWh, around the cost of electricity production.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The average USEP for the first quarter of this year has stabilised to around $360 per megawatt hour (MWh), around the cost of electricity production.

sections.label: EMA extending measures to June
sections.summary: Given the uncertain global energy situation, EMA will extend all measures, including TRECS, to end June 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Given the uncertain global energy situation, EMA will be extending all measures, including TRECS, to end June 2022.

sections.label: SP Group raising tariff rates
sections.summary: SP Group announced it would raise regulated tariff rates for its consumers by approximately 10%.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Last week, SP Group announced that it would be raising regulated tariff rates for its consumers by approximately 10%.

sections.label: Quadrupling solar deployment by 2030
sections.summary: Singapore will quadruple its solar deployment by 2030 to generate at least two gigawatt-peak of electricity by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the longer term, we will continue to diversify our energy sources.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will quadruple our solar deployment by 2030, to generate at least two gigawatt-peak of electricity by 2030.

sections.label: Importing low-carbon electricity by 2035
sections.summary: Singapore will continue to explore maximising solar potential and intends to import up to four gigawatt of low-carbon electricity by 2035.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will continue to explore ways to maximise Singapore's solar potential.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We also intend to import up to four gigawatt of low-carbon electricity by 2035.

sections.label: NTUC FairPrice discount initiatives
sections.summary: NTUC FairPrice has rolled out initiatives such as a 5% discount on 100 key essential items every Friday to help consumers stretch their dollar.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: For example, NTUC FairPrice has rolled out initiatives to help consumers stretch their dollar, such as by providing a 5% discount on 100 key essential items every Friday.

sections.label: Crude oil and fuel prices
sections.summary: As of end-March 2022, crude oil prices were about 40% higher than in January 2022, while petrol and diesel prices were about 15% and 30% higher respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: As of end-March 2022, crude oil prices were about 40% higher than in January 2022, while the price of petrol and diesel were, on average, about 15% and 30% higher respectively.

sections.label: CASE Price Kaki enhancement
sections.summary: CASE will enhance the Price Kaki application to enable users to compare the prices of similar items by their weight and volume.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: CASE will also enhance the Price Kaki application to enable users to compare the prices of similar items by their weight and volume.

sections.label: Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: The Small Business Recovery Grant provides $1,000 per local employee and up to $10,000 per firm, giving $175 million of support to small businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Small Business Recovery Grant provides $1,000 per local employee and up to $10,000 per firm.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: All in all, the Grant will provide $175 million of support to small businesses.

sections.label: Productivity Solutions Grant funding
sections.summary: In the Budget this year, around $600 million was set aside over the next four years under the Productivity Solutions Grant.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: In the Budget this year, we announced that we are setting aside around $600 million over the next four years under the Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG).

sections.label: Food Services and Retail Revitalisation Package
sections.summary: Minister of State Low Yen Ling announced the Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package to support food services and retail companies to improve productivity and stay competitive.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: At the Committee of Supply last month, Minister of State Low Yen Ling also announced the Food Services and Retail Business Revitalisation Package which will provide additional support to our food services and retail companies to improve their productivity, build the companies' capabilities to pivot and transform, hire and train more local workers and stay competitive and relevant.

sections.label: Global markets and FTAs
sections.summary: Singapore will strengthen economic integration and help enterprises use its FTA network, while safeguarding essential supplies and monitoring prices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Staying connected to global markets is essential to helping our businesses grow beyond our borders, attracting investments into Singapore and creating good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This is underpinned by our wide network of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), which create opportunities for our businesses in other regions and provide benefits, such as tariff savings, investment protection, amongst others.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We will continue to strengthen regional and international economic integration and help our enterprises, especially the SMEs, utilise and benefit from our network of FTAs.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But, make no mistake, we will continue to safeguard the security of our essential supplies, such as energy and food, and refresh our strategies for a more resilient economy.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Three, we will closely monitor price movements and will not hesitate to take enforcement action against anti-competitive behaviour.

sections.label: ComCare extension and reapplication
sections.summary: ComCare SMTA will be extended for new and existing applicants, and the process streamlined, but extensions will not be made automatic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will the Minister consider making these extensions automatic, so that both the recipients and also our civil servants and SSOs can do away with the administrative burden of having to reapply, renew, find justifications and so on, which could go a long way towards reducing the stresses that people are facing at this very difficult time?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we are already going to extend ComCare for a minimum duration of six months for all new ComCare SMTA applicants and extend ComCare SMTA by another three months for those who require further assistance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The question is: why not make that automatic?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, at this stage, rather than making it automatic, for those who need it, they will get it and that is the assurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And we will streamline the process, make it easy for them to apply, there is no need to re-submit so many different documents all over again, it should not be a burden to them, nor should it create stress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For those who need it, the assurance is that the support will be given to them.

sections.label: Car ownership and revenue
sections.summary: Giving up revenue sources should be considered carefully, and only four in 10 Singaporean households own cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, we should think carefully about giving up these sources of revenue, particularly when we are facing considerable revenue challenges already and we had a long discussion in the Budget debate about all the revenue and fiscal challenges we face.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as I have highlighted, only four in 10 Singaporean households own cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For the bottom 20%, one in 10; for the top 20%, it is six in 10.

sections.label: GST offset and cost of living
sections.summary: The AP will delay the impact of GST by at least five years for the majority of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: More than just a GST offset, it also addresses cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why the AP will delay the impact of GST by at least five years, for the majority of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Brochure on household help
sections.summary: A brochure shows Singaporeans the help coming in the year ahead, including a $150 monthly utility rebate for a 4-room household.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And that is what we have tried to do in the brochure, to pull it together to show Singaporeans, in one "simple-to-understand" way, all the help that will be coming up in the year ahead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And, to illustrate, for a 4-room household, we are talking about $150 a month of utility rebate this month.

sections.label: Budget support and profiteering
sections.summary: The Budget should be rolled out and implemented, and profiteering is guarded against through a multi-pronged approach beyond CAP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But for now, let us roll out and properly implement all that is in the Budget already, which is already giving considerable support to households.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We guard against profiteering through a multi-pronged approach that goes beyond CAP, because this includes promoting competition, helping consumers make informed decisions and encouraging a very diversified supply chain.

sections.label: Publishing errant GST-profiteering businesses
sections.summary: CAP may make public errant businesses that profiteer on the pretext of the GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: CAP may also make public errant businesses that seek to profiteer on the pretext of GST increase to account for it.

sections.label: Duty for greener transport
sections.summary: An externality point is that the duty is needed to go greener and embrace more energy-efficient transport modes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The second point, from an externality point of view, we do need to have that duty in place in order to, as we all talked about, go greener, wanting to embrace more energy-efficient modes of transport, a point which everyone supported, incidentally, in this House, not too long ago.

sections.label: EMA calibrated electricity price increase
sections.summary: EMA collectively looks at wheeling charges, grid charges, fuel and non-fuel costs to come up with a calibrated price increase.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We are exposed to global energy prices and, when oil prices rise, electricity prices will, of course, rise in tandem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But, collectively, EMA looks at the wheeling charges, looks at multiple components, including the grid charges, fuel price components directly attributable to fuel costs, the procurement of fuel costs, and the non-fuel costs and then, collectively, come up with a calibrated price increase.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme support
sections.summary: The Government set aside a significant sum through the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme to help companies transition and alleviate costs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: On top of that, to support businesses, to alleviate the cost of this Progressive Wage Model, the Government has also put aside a significant sum of money to help companies transition by the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme.

sections.label: SGUnited programme permanent fixture
sections.summary: The SGUnited programme for mid-career and older workers will be made a permanent fixture of policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Through all of our SGUnited programmes, as I have shared earlier on, for the mid-career, for the older workers, we will make the SGUnited programme a permanent fixture of our policy.

sections.label: Inflation impact on real incomes
sections.summary: The Government looks at inflation's impact on groups and real incomes, but cannot fix nominal wages or guarantee positive real incomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We look at the impact of inflation on different groups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And on real incomes, I think it is important to highlight it is not possible for the Government to fix nominal wages, to guarantee that real incomes will always be positive.

sections.label: Monitoring and readiness to do more
sections.summary: The Government will monitor the situation closely and stands ready to do more if it worsens externally and in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, there are all these different considerations and that is why we cannot so simply distil it to just one key parameter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the assurance that we continue to give is, we will monitor this very closely and, should there be a worsening of the situation externally and within Singapore, we will, certainly, stand ready to do more.

sections.label: Flexibility, longer contracts, subsidy difficulty
sections.summary: Flexibility and longer contracts with Sembawang and Keppel give predictability, but subsidising a lower price tier would be difficult.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, the flexibility that we give in providing monthly and then, separately, we went on to talk to, as I have shared just now, Sembawang and Keppel, to provide longer contracts – six months, one year, two years, up to three years – provides a lot more predictability and some level of certainty, albeit not back to what it was before.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: I guess the part that we are in this difficult position is, if you are saying that you want to have a separate tier, a lower tier, then that price differential has to be subsidised by someone, right?

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Perhaps I may be getting it wrong – the Member can clarify.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: But if the Member is suggesting that the Government steps in to subsidise that component, then I think it will be very difficult because electricity power consumption is one of those things: how do you subsidise that when people will then just keep consuming more?

sections.label: Budget packages and Small Business Recovery Grant
sections.summary: Budget packages cushion consumers and the Small Business Recovery Grant applies to all SMEs in affected sectors, including logistics and delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And as I mentioned, we have helped to cushion the impact on consumers also through different packages that we have in the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We also have a Small Business Recovery Grant that will be applied to all SMEs who are in the affected sectors, including people who are running logistics, delivery.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: As I said earlier, let us monitor the effects of all that we are doing, how it percolates through the economy before we decide on our next steps.

sections.label: Wage-price spiral and careful interventions
sections.summary: The risk of a wage-price spiral is real, so future Government interventions must be designed carefully and Budget measures implemented and monitored first.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On Mr Liang Eng Hwa's point, he is absolutely right that we have to watch carefully the dynamics which he talked about, a wage-price spiral potentially taking place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: For example, the opening up of borders will allow more migrant workers to come in, particularly in some of the hard-pressed sectors like construction, marine and process, and this will help ease the situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But the risk of a wage-price spiral taking place is real and that is why it also means we have to be very careful in designing any future Government interventions, because, if we are not careful, the Government spends more and this feeds into wages and then it may inflate prices and wages, and it may cause inflation to be worse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why, as I mentioned just now, the basic strategy and approach are to let whatever we have announced in the Budget, which is already very generous, get implemented properly first, monitor the effects on the economy before we consider next steps, taking into consideration at that time the wider economic situation externally, the economic situation within Singapore and, for that matter, our own fiscal situation.

sections.label: CAP focus on essentials
sections.summary: CAP focuses on essential food items commonly consumed by Singaporean households and non-food essentials such as household products.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: CAP's focus is on the essential food items commonly consumed by Singaporean households and non-food essentials, such as household products.
